metadata.title: Unfolding key factors of resilience in ICT cognitive-motivational engagement: Global evidence from machine learning techniques

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata merged across student, teacher, and school questionnaires, then constructs a binary resilience outcome based on within-country ESCS quartiles and cross-country ICT engagement quartiles. The manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling weights or any replicate-weight scheme (e.g., BRR/jackknife), and the ML pipeline is implemented in Python with scikit-learn/imbalanced-learn. Because the paper does not discuss complex survey design adjustments, the reported classification performance should be interpreted as model discrimination on the analytic sample rather than as population-representative estimates. Preprocessing includes kNN imputation, min-max normalization to [0,1], and SMOTETomek resampling to address class imbalance, but no survey-weight-aware resampling or weighting is described.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: plausible_values_handling is 'not_applicable' — the study likely does not analyze cognitive achievement PVs (e.g., it may focus on affective/attitudinal outcomes, curriculum data, or non-ILSA micro-data).

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2018 students from the 53 countries/economies that administered the optional ICT familiarity questionnaire. Defined the analytic population as ESCS-disadvantaged students (bottom quarter of ESCS within each country/economy), yielding 68,959 students. Further classified resilience in ICT engagement by selecting those whose ICT engagement is in the top quarter across the 53 countries/economies, producing 13,418 ICT engagement resilient students (IRS) and 55,541 non-ICT engagement resilient students (NRS).

confounders_identified.variable_name: Ability to adapt to new situations

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 (53 economies) ICT familiarity questionnaire — resilience in ICT engagement (binary classification)
main_findings.target_variable: Resilience in ICT engagement (IRS vs NRS)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Logistic Regression (LR): AUC=74.05%, Accuracy=68.13%, Recall=72.29%, Precision=67.14%, F-measure=69.51%. Decision Tree (DT): AUC=84.84%, Accuracy=76.57%, Recall=75.19%, Precision=76.67%, F-measure=75.07%. Random Forest (RF): AUC=94.81%, Accuracy=86.86%, Recall=84.67%, Precision=88.18%, F-measure=84.70%. SVM: AUC=95.10%, Accuracy=86.45%, Recall=97.09%, Precision=80.27%, F-measure=87.78%. Best by F-measure: SVM (87.78%).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 (53 economies) ICT familiarity questionnaire the study leveraged ICT use outside school, ICT resources at home, self-efficacy, gender, and parents’ emotional support to classify resilience in ICT engagement (IRS vs NRS), finding that SVM achieved the highest F-measure (87.78%) and very high recall (97.09%) compared with LR and DT. This indicates that strengthening ICT-related motivational and support factors—especially those linked to out-of-school ICT use and self-efficacy—may improve the identification and targeting of ESCS-disadvantaged students who can sustain high ICT engagement, though the cross-sectional design and lack of survey-weight reporting limit causal interpretation.

data.outcome_summary: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata from 53 countries/economies that administered the optional ICT familiarity questionnaire to classify students as ICT engagement resilient (IRS) versus non-resilient (NRS). Resilience is defined as ESCS in the bottom quarter within each country/economy combined with ICT engagement in the top quarter across the 53 economies, yielding 68,959 students (13,418 IRS; 55,541 NRS). Four supervised ML classifiers—Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and SVM—are trained using a preprocessing pipeline that includes kNN imputation, min-max normalization, and SMOTETomek to address class imbalance, evaluated with 10-fold cross-validation using Accuracy, AUC, Recall, Precision, and F-measure. SVM performs best overall by F-measure (87.78%) and achieves the highest recall (97.09%), while RF shows the highest precision (88.18%) and strong AUC (94.81%). The manuscript does not report applying PISA sampling/replicate weights, and the study is cross-sectional, so results should be interpreted as predictive discrimination rather than causal effects.
